document.title: Delivery DNA 1.0.0 Question Catalogue
document.approvalAuthority: Product Owner and Chief Solution Architect

journey.title: Delivery DNA assessment
journey.introduction: Delivery DNA looks at how your organisation enables, manages and learns from delivery. Answer for how things work today, using the best evidence available.
journey.instructions: Choose the option that most closely reflects your organisation today. Consider relevant delivery activity across the organisation, not one exceptional project. If you cannot support a response, leave it unanswered rather than estimate. Use Not applicable only where the question genuinely does not apply and explain why.

dimensionInstructions.foundation: Consider whether the necessary purpose, ownership, roles and agreed approach are clearly established and current.
dimensionInstructions.practice: Consider what routinely happens across relevant delivery activity, not isolated examples or stated intent.
dimensionInstructions.evidence: Consider recent, verifiable records, decisions, measures or outcomes rather than confidence or anecdote alone.

options.label: Not in place
options.description: Little or no consistent evidence is available.

options.label: Emerging
options.description: Some examples exist, but they are informal, isolated or inconsistent.

options.label: Defined
options.description: An agreed approach exists and is used in important areas, but application varies.

options.label: Consistent
options.description: The approach is used consistently across most relevant delivery activity and is supported by current evidence.

options.label: Embedded
options.description: The approach is embedded across relevant delivery activity, reviewed and improved using evidence.

not_applicable.label: Not applicable
not_applicable.reasonPrompt: Briefly explain why this question does not apply to your organisation.
not_applicable.customerHelp: Use this only when the question genuinely does not apply. It is not scored and may limit the result.

missing.label: Not answered
missing.customerHelp: This question is not scored. Missing required evidence may reduce confidence or make part of the result unavailable.

completionPolicy.missingAcknowledgement: Some questions are not answered. You can complete the assessment, but this may limit the results and reduce confidence.

questions.prompt: How clearly are the organisation's delivery priorities and intended outcomes defined and connected to its strategy?
How consistently are delivery decisions and trade-offs made using those strategic priorities and intended outcomes?
How consistently can leaders see evidence that delivery activity is contributing to the intended strategic outcomes?
How clearly are decision rights, governance forums and escalation routes defined for delivery?
How consistently do governance forums make timely decisions, resolve issues and hold delivery to account?
How consistently is there evidence that governance decisions are recorded, acted on and followed through?
How clearly are executive sponsors, their responsibilities and accountabilities defined for delivery?
How consistently do executive sponsors provide direction, remove barriers and own key decisions?
How consistently is there evidence that sponsor actions and decisions are followed through in delivery?
How clearly are portfolio objectives, prioritisation criteria and investment boundaries defined?
How consistently is work prioritised, started, stopped or rebalanced using agreed criteria and available capacity?
How consistently is there evidence that portfolio choices reflect strategic value, constraints and delivery performance?
How clearly are programme outcomes, governance, dependencies and delivery approach defined?
How consistently are programme-level dependencies, risks, decisions and delivery plans actively managed?
How consistently is there evidence that programmes are progressing against agreed outcomes, milestones and dependencies?
How clearly are project outcomes, scope, responsibilities and delivery approach defined?
How consistently are projects planned, monitored, adapted and closed using agreed controls?
How consistently is there evidence that projects deliver agreed outputs and outcomes within understood constraints?
How clearly are planning standards, baselines, controls and change tolerances defined?
How consistently are plans maintained, forecasts updated and changes controlled using current information?
How consistently is there reliable evidence of progress, forecast accuracy, changes and corrective action?
How clearly are intended benefits, measures, owners and realisation timescales defined?
How consistently are benefits tracked, reviewed and acted on through delivery and after implementation?
How consistently is there evidence that benefit measures are being achieved or that corrective action is taken?
How clearly are delivery risk, assurance, control and escalation expectations defined?
How consistently are risks, assumptions, issues and assurance findings identified, challenged and acted on?
How consistently is there evidence that material risks and assurance actions are current, owned and resolved or accepted?
How clearly are affected stakeholders, change impacts, engagement needs and adoption outcomes defined?
How consistently are stakeholders engaged and change impacts prepared for, supported and monitored?
How consistently is there evidence of stakeholder understanding, adoption and sustained use of delivered changes?
How clearly are the PMO's purpose, service offer, authority and relationship with delivery teams defined?
How consistently does the PMO provide proportionate support, challenge, coordination and standards?
How consistently is there evidence that PMO services are used and associated with clearer decisions, visibility and delivery discipline?
How clearly are reporting purposes, measures, ownership and data standards defined?
How consistently is delivery information updated, validated and used in decisions?
How consistently is there evidence that reports are timely, reliable and provide actionable insight rather than activity-only updates?
How clearly are improvement responsibilities, feedback routes and learning expectations defined?
How consistently are delivery lessons, performance signals and feedback translated into agreed improvements?
How consistently is there evidence that improvement actions are completed, reviewed and embedded in subsequent delivery?
